title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page is part of the 'equation des lacets' analysis around the (profinite) modular group. PSL(2,Z) is the free product Z/3 * Z/2, generated by rho = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (order 3 mod ±1) and sigma = [[0,-1],[1,0]] (order 2 mod ±1). The script G is a profinite quotient of SL(2,Z)^ (or of its ±1 quotient).

G_{rho,sigma} appears to be an extension of a small finite group gamma_{rho,sigma} by G, through delta_G : G_{rho,sigma} -> gamma_{rho,sigma} with kernel G. This reading is supported by the next page, where SZ_rho = Ker delta_rho = Z_rho ∩ G. Its elements act on G, including 'orientation-reversing' elements of GL_2 with det = -1, such as tau'_inf = tau·sigma, which inverts rho, and tau_inf, which inverts sigma. gamma_{rho,sigma} has two distinguished subgroups gamma' and gamma''. From formula (32) on the previous page, Z_rho and Z_sigma are the centralizers of rho and sigma in G_{rho,sigma}, and delta_rho, delta_sigma are the restrictions of delta_G.

Proposition.
1) delta_rho(Z_rho) always contains gamma'. It equals gamma' exactly when rho and rho^{-1} are not conjugate in G; otherwise it is all of gamma. So delta_rho is surjective iff rho ~ rho^{-1} in G.
2) The same holds for sigma, with sigma^{-1} = -sigma.
The mechanism: if h in G conjugates rho to rho^{-1}, then composing h with an inverting element of determinant -1 gives an element of Z_rho whose image lies outside gamma'.

Corollary: if G surjects onto SL(2,Z/3)' (= PSL(2,F_3) ≅ A_4), then Im delta_rho = gamma'. One must show rho is conjugate to neither rho^{-1} nor -rho^{-1} in SL(2,F_3).
- rho has trace 1 and -rho^{-1} has trace -1, so those two are excluded.
- For rho^{-1}: tau'_inf = tau·sigma inverts rho and has det -1. The centralizer of rho in M_2(F_3) is F_3[rho]. So every conjugator in GL_2(F_3) taking rho to rho^{-1} has the form f·tau'_inf with f = c·rho + d.
- Determinant 1 forces det f = c^2 + cd + d^2 = -1.
- The norm form x^2 + xy + y^2 takes only the values 0 and 1 mod 3, so this is impossible.

The next page does the parallel case for sigma with SL(2,Z/4): one needs t^2 + u^2 = -1 mod 4, which is impossible.

Purpose: to decide whether the centralizers of the elliptic generators surject onto the 'sign/orientation' group. This matters for describing solutions of the loop equations (GT-type actions on SL(2,Z)^ / Gamma_{1,1}) up to these symmetries. The upshot is that the obstructions are 3-adic for rho and 2-adic for sigma. They therefore persist in SL(2,Z^) itself and in the universal SL(2,Z)^.
errors: The crossed-out lines on the previous page suggested that sigma is conjugate to -sigma in SL(2,Z^) ('par la théorie de Steinberg'). That is false: it would need t^2 + u^2 = -1 in Z_2, impossible mod 4. Grothendieck evidently caught this; the next page proves non-conjugacy via SL(2,Z/4).

The phrase 'rho et ±rho^{-1}' with 'traces distinctes 1 et -1' only settles -rho^{-1}. rho^{-1} has the same trace as rho, which is why the separate determinant/norm-form argument follows. The page's argument is complete, though, and the computation is correct.

ideas.what: Image of the centralizer of an elliptic generator in the outer 'sign' group is controlled by whether the generator is conjugate to its inverse
ideas.modern_name: Real vs non-real conjugacy classes; centralizer/normalizer exact sequence for orientation-reversing automorphisms

ideas.what: Non-conjugacy of rho and rho^{-1} detected mod 3 via the norm form c^2 + cd + d^2; non-conjugacy of sigma and sigma^{-1} detected mod 4 via t^2 + u^2
ideas.modern_name: Local (3-adic / 2-adic) obstruction to conjugacy in SL_2; ideal classes / norm forms of Z[zeta_3] and Z[i]
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Latimer–MacDuffee type counting, conjugacy in SL_2)

deep.surprise_reason: These are correct but routine finite-group computations serving Grothendieck's internal bookkeeping of the loop-equation symmetries for SL(2,Z)^. The 2-adic/3-adic obstruction observation is elementary and known.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: '[-..-] {+v+}ide si et seulement si : gamma' ssi' should read roughly 'et est identique à gamma'_{rho,sigma} ssi rho et rho^{-1} non conjugués dans G'.
'1 et -1, et Z/3Z, ils ne sont pas conjugués' likely reads '1 et -1, et [dans SL(2,Z/3Z)]...' — the arrangement is uncertain.
'Or (tau sigma)(rho) = rho^{-1}' has 'tau'_inf' written under 'tau sigma' as its name, i.e. tau'_inf := tau·sigma.
'{+identifiés là :+}' is above a crossed-out word; probably '[vérifi]cations là'.
Last line: '(car det(tau'_inf) = -1) i.e. c^2 + cd + d^2 = -1, impossible' — the transcription is correct.
